title: About HART
lede: HART Railroad is an HO scale model railroad of Neville Island, the industrial island in the Ohio River just downstream of Pittsburgh. The places, industries, and connecting railroads are real. HART itself, and its Pittsburgh & Chartiers Valley Division, are our own.

sections.heading: What HART is
paragraphs: From 1899 until January 31, 1994, the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway switched the island's furnaces, coke ovens, and interchange. HART is modeled as its successor: the railroad that takes over that job once the P&OV is gone.

HART handles the interchange between CSX and the Pittsburgh & Ohio Central (POHC) and switches the industries on the island. South Yard is where the two connections meet and where most of the sorting gets done.

sections.heading: Prototype target
paragraphs: The island between 1994, when the P&OV shut down, and January 2016, when Shenango Coke Works made its last coke.
bullets: CSX local D749 works the island from Demmler and McKeesport.
The POHC comes over from Scully Yard and McKees Rocks, often waiting for D749 to clear the trestle over the Ohio.
Customers: Aristech Plastics, A. Stucki Company, Calgon Carbon, Ferrellgas, Kosmos Cement, and Shenango Coke Works.
Signals are Chessie / early CSX searchlights: 13 two-head searchlights and 10 dwarfs.
Not prototype: HART and the P&CV Division are invented, and Route 23, a PCC streetcar crossing the island, is a liberty.

sections.heading: Aims
bullets: Operations that feel like a real railroad, not a pile of car cards.
Shipper-driven traffic: shippers create demand, the railroad fills it with cars, and the paperwork follows the move. Traffic and waybills come from STS, the Shipper-driven Traffic Simulator.

A track scale at South Yard. Coke hoppers from Shenango are weighed mid-move, and cars that are overloaded or out of balance go back for a reload, the practice AAR General Information Bulletin No. 5 describes.
A dispatcher running Digicon-style CTC with working signals in the aisle.
Repeatable sessions: each session is saved as a recipe, so it can be rerun, tuned, or handed to someone else.
A small roster where every car earns its keep.

links.label: Setting up car movement with STS

sections.heading: Where the layout stands (October 2026)
bullets: Operating sessions have started. Session #2 was the first run with STS traffic, car cards, and waybills.
Control runs on JMRI, with turnouts and occupancy detection reported over MQTT.
CATS provides the Digicon CTC and ABS panels. JMRI Signal Mast Logic sets the aspects, and LCOS drives the LED searchlights. Signal rules are still being tuned.
The Neville Island helix is under construction.
